title: Euclidean Distance Geometry
abstract: Develops the basepoint-centered Gram approach to finite Euclidean distance geometry. Proves both directions of Schoenberg's characterization, including a rank-controlled factorization of positive-semidefinite matrices; proves that three affinely independent centers in Euclidean three-space determine at most two points with prescribed distances; and verifies the Cayley--Menger determinant for segments and triangles, including the triangle-area identity underlying Heron's formula.

informal.DistanceGeometry.schoenberg: For n at least one, a symmetric hollow n-by-n matrix is a squared-distance matrix of points in k-dimensional Euclidean space exactly when its basepoint-centered Gram matrix is positive semidefinite and has rank at most k.
informal.DistanceGeometry.encard_setOf_forall_dis: In a finite-dimensional real inner-product affine space, prescribed distances to centers whose affine span has codimension one admit at most two solutions.
informal.DistanceGeometry.trilateration_le_two: Three affinely independent centers in three-dimensional Euclidean space admit at most two points with any prescribed triple of distances.
informal.DistanceGeometry.cayleyMenger_det_heron: The Cayley--Menger determinant of three planar points equals minus sixteen times the squared area of their triangle.
